_meta.title: B remaining #549-586 evidence notes
_meta.source: Reviewed original eight-source archives and targeted current web checks; official references verify geographic or access facts, not cruising activity.

items.description_rewritten: Cranford Country Park is a Hillingdon council woodland and historic estate beside the River Crane. The physical park is confirmed, but the old directory's activity claim is not current; a 2008 report documented robberies targeting visitors years ago.

McKee's Dam is a council recreation area near Hillsborough/Dromore. A 2016 local news article described complaints about sexual encounters; its age makes it historical evidence only. A June 2026 directory comment asks whether anyone still visits, not a confirmed visit.

recent_online.description: An online directory commenter asked whether anyone still visits; the question is not an encounter report.

items.description_rewritten: Forest Road is a vague name for a roadside/wooded location near Limavady. A Gays-Cruising page is independently indexed, but a reliable exact junction, permitted parking and recent activity remain unresolved. Cam and Springwell are separate forests and must not be assumed identical.

Liverpool Street is a major managed rail station in London. Network Rail confirms ordinary passenger toilets, while a 2026 redevelopment approval means legacy descriptions may no longer match layouts. The two directory references are not dated witness evidence.

The directory name 'Cruising in Dark Garden' does not specify a recognisable named public garden in London. Do not replace it with an unrelated park or fabricate coordinates. Its source-country listing exists, but the site's identity and present access are unknown.

London Waterloo is a working National Rail station in Southwark. Network Rail confirms customer toilets and a lower-concourse retail complex, but the original cruising index does not establish which facility, date or current activity.

Carnaby Street's underground council-managed public toilets are explicitly listed by Westminster for reopening in early 2027. Treat historic cruising guide mentions as non-current and the facilities as unavailable at the November 2026 research date.

The British Library at St Pancras provides public visitor facilities, while research reading rooms on floors 1–3 require a Reader Pass. A travel guide mentioning Level 3 toilets is not evidence that any specific visitor can access those rooms or that cruising presently happens.

Victoria is an operating major London railway terminus with passenger toilets, accessible and Changing Places facilities. No firsthand 2025–2026 reports corroborate the travel-guide's reference to main-concourse toilets.

The likely intended property is Hilton London Tower Bridge at 5 More London Place near London Bridge; the original guide says Hilton London Bridge without an exact hotel identity. The hotel is real, but access to private customer facilities and any sexual-use claim are unverified.

One New Change is a shopping destination near St Paul's in the City. The older guide alleges activity in shopping-centre toilets, not an adult venue. Current access to its specific lower-ground/first-floor facilities and any recent activity have not been corroborated.

Dickens Square is a public residential park around Harper Road in Southwark. CruisingGays supplies a historic directory entry but no accessible dated 2025–2026 witness; preserve the park name without inferring present crowd patterns.

Woolwich Riverwalk denotes an imprecise public Thames-side walking area. The archival CruisingGays source mentions the Thames Barrier area but must not be conflated with Thames Barrier Park across the river on the Newham bank.

'Canal Tow Path' is too broad to geolocate safely. The historic source places the suggestion near Green Lanes/Manor House, but does not establish the exact watercourse or path segment. Avoid coordinates until the identity is independently pinned.

The northern Thames Path segment between Blackfriars and Millennium bridges is a legitimate public riverside walkway. City of London completed the Globe View connection in 2023; the old report's secluded layout descriptions may now be obsolete.

Broadgate's retail/business complex by Liverpool Street has changed over time, and the old CruisingGays description of lower-level toilets cannot be confirmed as a currently identifiable facility. Managed commercial property, not a dedicated cruise venue.

The Barbican arts complex has gendered, gender-neutral and accessible public facilities on multiple levels. The operator publishes updated toilet locations. An old generic directory listing must not be treated as an identified contemporary play area.

Bishopsgate Institute is an active cultural and education building at 230 Bishopsgate, with reading-room hours varying by day. CruisingGays and Splashd both mention its toilets, but neither provides verifiable 2025–2026 eyewitness activity.

Eastcheap is a street in the City of London, not the name of a specific public convenience. The CruisingGays reference is insufficient to identify an operating toilet. Do not infer that public facilities at another Eastcheap address are the same place.

The National Archives visitor site is at Kew in west London, not the City centre. The archival directory mentions visitor restrooms but offers no recent verification, and ordinary public institution facilities are not adult spaces.

The former Truman Brewery estate at 91 Brick Lane is an active commercial and event complex. Its official security notice describes continuous security and CCTV. Access to any upper-floor washrooms cited historically is not established.

City Thameslink is a working Thameslink station at Ludgate Hill. National Rail confirms toilet facilities, but different rail information providers disagree on availability. The older CruisingGays and newer undated Splashd descriptions do not verify current cruising.

Thames Barrier Park is a Newham public park in the Royal Docks by Pontoon Dock DLR, with lawns and family facilities. It is on the north bank and distinct from Woolwich Riverwalk. Official park information confirms recreational access, not cruising.

A Glenshane lay-by near Maghera is explicitly subject to a Department for Infrastructure road-access prohibition from 8 January 2024 for the western entrance opposite Ranaghan Road. The archive does not prove this is the same lay-by as the cruising-directory suggestion.

Ragged Hall Lane is a road near St Albans. The old directory labels a natural area without a clearly identified public woodland or right of access. Treat the precise location and current activity as unresolved rather than mapping private land.

Horsenden Hill is Ealing's extensive green space in Perivale, with woodland, meadows and council-described parking off Horsenden Lane North. The specific car-park claim is undated and should not be presented as current activity.

The Thur bank opposite Alten sits within the wider Thurauen landscape near Flaach; its nature centre identifies an Alten car park within a protected reserve. The original directory wording is a rough area clue only; permitted access and exact spot require checking.

'Parkplatz Arlesheim' is a generic parking-area label in Arlesheim near Basel, not a unique site. A July 2026 original-source check-in was logged but lacks independent physical activity evidence; do not infer active cruising from a click or check-in.

recent_online.description: Archive flags a July 2026 check-in but no verifiable physical encounter.

items.description_rewritten: The Bern Allmend area near Wankdorf is confirmed as an old CruisingGays entry and is plausibly the same broad park described as 'Allmend Anhöhe'. Its archived details cannot establish reliable present activity or any legal permission for public sexual activity.

Mägenwil municipality confirms its Birretholz forestry administration in the Mägenwil/Birrhard area. This supports regional woodland identity only, not a specifically bounded 'Mägenwilerwald' cruising site or dated visitor reports.

Meienried's Alte Aare is part of a protected Bernese floodplain with sensitive bank vegetation and seasonal restrictions on leaving marked paths. Government documentation confirms the nature reserve but no recent cruising.

Rastplatz Oberengstringen is a motorway rest area by the A1 in the Zurich/Limmat corridor, with a long history of proposed redesign and access disputes. Its place identity is plausible but no recent gay activity or exact permitted pedestrian access is verified.

'Kempthal' appears to be a broad/misspelled reference to Kemptthal, the rail-side former Maggi industrial area now branded The Valley. It is not a verified park or single site; the directory's exact intended wooded area is unresolved.

Wanneholz at 6034 Inwil is a named wooded place according to the directory, but no independently confirmed exact boundary, access regulations, or activity reports were located in this research pass. Retain as an unresolved original candidate.

Zurich Airport's P3 is an operating paid parking building directly linked to Check-in 3. The archive names 'WC Fflughafen P3' with a typo; airport parking operations are verified but the specific toilet and any cruising claim are not.

Lucerne's Inseliquai/Inseli public-toilet facilities appear in the municipal WC inventory near the station. Two cruising directories refer to an Inseli/Lucerne location, but historic and current access details may differ and no dated recent witness report was verified.

Ufschötti is a lakeside recreation area at Alpenquai with beach, lawns and WC facilities. Official Luzern tourism guidance describes summer access and a seasonal closure from early November to Easter, making November activity assumptions especially unreliable.
items.operational_status: official seasonal closure early November through Easter

items.description_rewritten: Bundesplatz is a public square in Lucerne and has appeared in an earlier city WC inventory. The source queue contains both a Gays-Cruising entry and Squirt record for this candidate; neither supplies verified 2025–2026 firsthand activity. Confirm exact facility before publication.
